# Build Agent — Operating Manual v1 (CEO-readable end-to-end) **Version:** v1.0.0 **Date:** 2026-04-25 **Audience:** Marc — this is the plain-English walkthrough of how the Build Agent works from your message to a LIVE shipped agent. --- ## What you're getting One agent — the Build Agent — that builds every other agent in your fleet. You talk to it through Claude using one of four templates (Build, Work, Approve, Activate). It runs on Windmill, calls Anthropic, gets reviewed by KRITE, ships a real test-fired runtime, and self-promotes to LIVE only after a week of real traces. No more spec-only "builds." No more drift. --- ## The 7-step pipeline ### Step 1 — Intake You type one of the four templates. Claude (your orchestrator) parses the XML tags into a structured payload. Required fields are validated. If anything's missing, Claude asks you exactly which field — not a generic "tell me more." **Plain English:** you say what you want using a fill-in form. Claude doesn't guess. If you skip a required field, Claude asks for it. ### Step 2 — Research-first Build Agent fires a research worker (Daniel pattern, Perplexity sonar-pro). Worker finds 2-3 industry winners in the relevant silo. Pulls their actual templates. Cites T1 sources. **Plain English:** before building, Build Agent looks at how Ryan Serhant, Tom Ferry, Andrew Huberman, etc. actually do this thing. Their playbook becomes the starting point — adapted to your voice and silo. ### Step 3 — Adapt + WKU pass Strip the winner's branding. Re-voice for your tone. Re-scope for your silo (no multi-tenant, no sellable surfaces). Apply Wisdom-Knowledge-Understanding test. **Plain English:** Build Agent rewrites the winners' template in your voice, makes sure it serves YOUR three companies (not "external CRG clients"), and checks three questions: is this the right call, is it accurate, does it connect the dots. ### Step 4 — Build runtime Write the actual code. TypeScript or Python in Windmill, or Anthropic SDK script, or Vapi config. Save to disk. Verify the file exists with a directory listing. **Plain English:** real code. Saved to a real file. We can prove it exists. ### Step 5 — Test-fire Run the agent ONCE with a representative input. Capture the output (first 500 chars). Capture the Langfuse trace ID. **Plain English:** Build Agent actually invokes the new agent — it doesn't just write the file and hope. The first run produces evidence we can show you. ### Step 6 — KRITE review Hand the artifact to KRITE for 5-axis scoring (voice, compliance, research, tone, WKU). KRITE uses Haiku — cheap and fast. Threshold is 0.80 on every axis. - All 5 axes ≥ 0.80 → proceed to Step 7. - Any axis < 0.80 → Build Agent re-fires Step 3 with KRITE's feedback. Max 3 iterations. - 3 iterations failed → escalate to you with full trace. **Plain English:** a separate reviewer checks the work before we report success. If the work fails review, Build Agent revises automatically. If it can't get it right after 3 tries, you get pinged. ### Step 7 — Ship as BUILT Return the Gate D contract: runtime file path + size, test-fire command, test-fire output, Langfuse trace ID, KRITE scores, doctrine refs applied, and a plain-English summary for you. **Plain English:** you receive a one-paragraph English summary of what got built and what it does. The technical evidence is at the bottom or in a .docx link. ### Step 8 (later) — Self-promote to LIVE Build Agent does NOT promote to LIVE. After 7 days of real Langfuse traces (Gate A doctrine), Samuel's weekly digest sees the activity, marks the agent LIVE in memory, and reports the promotion in your Monday morning brief. **Plain English:** "BUILT" means it works once. "LIVE" means it's been running successfully for a week. The transition is automatic — no theater, no premature celebration. --- ## Visual flow (Mermaid diagram — renders in many tools) ```mermaid flowchart TD Marc["Marc types a template
(Build / Work / Approve / Activate)"] --> Claude["Claude orchestrator
parses XML tags"] Claude -->|"validation fails"| Refusal["REFUSE
ask for missing field"] Claude -->|"validation OK"| Windmill["Windmill flow
fires Build Agent"] Windmill --> Research["Step 2: Research worker
(Daniel pattern / Perplexity)"] Research --> Adapt["Step 3: Adapt + WKU pass"] Adapt --> Build["Step 4: Build runtime
(write file, verify)"] Build --> TestFire["Step 5: Test-fire
(invoke once, capture trace)"] TestFire --> KRITE["Step 6: KRITE review
(5-axis, Haiku judge)"] KRITE -->|"all axes >= 0.80"| Ship["Step 7: Ship BUILT
Gate D contract returned"] KRITE -->|"any axis < 0.80
iteration < 3"| Adapt KRITE -->|"3 iterations failed"| Escalate["Escalate to Marc
with full trace"] Ship --> MarcReport["Marc receives plain-English
outcome summary"] MarcReport --> Wait["7 days of Langfuse traces"] Wait --> Samuel["Samuel weekly digest
auto-promotes BUILT -> LIVE"] Samuel --> MorningBrief["Monday morning brief
announces LIVE status"] ``` --- ## Cost expectation per build | Step | Token spend (est) | Notes | |------|-------------------|-------| | Step 2 — Research | ~$0.03 | Perplexity sonar-pro, 1-2 calls | | Step 3 — Adapt | ~$0.05 | Sonnet, 1 pass | | Step 4 — Build | ~$0.10 | Sonnet, 1-2 passes | | Step 5 — Test-fire | ~$0.01 | Whatever the agent itself uses | | Step 6 — KRITE | ~$0.005 | Haiku, 5 axes | | Iterations (avg 1) | ~$0.10 | Re-do steps 3-6 | | **Total per build** | **~$0.30** | Order of magnitude | A full week of 10 builds = ~$3. Compare to Cognition AI / Devin which charges hundreds per build. Marc's stack is cost-disciplined by construction. --- ## What can go wrong + what happens | Failure | What Build Agent does | |---------|-----------------------| | Research returns no T1 sources | Re-fire research once. If still empty, escalate to Marc. | | Code file fails to write | Retry with explicit absolute path. If still fails, return FAILED with error details. | | Test-fire returns 5xx | Retry once. If still fails, debug-mode runs — captures full stack trace, reports back. | | KRITE fails iteration 1 | Re-fire Step 3 with feedback injected. | | KRITE fails iteration 3 | Escalate. Marc gets the artifact + KRITE rationale + decision options. | | Marc requests build outside doctrine | Refuse with citation of conflicting doctrine file. | | Schedule never fires (BUILT but not LIVE after 14 days) | Samuel digest flags as orphan. Marc decides to fix or kill. | --- ## How this prevents the theater pattern Per `feedback_theater_pattern_named.md` — "spec declared live without runtime evidence" was the recurring failure. This pipeline prevents it three ways: 1. **No build is BUILT without a test-fire.** Step 5 is mandatory. Build Agent literally cannot return BUILT without a captured Langfuse trace ID. 2. **No build is LIVE without 7 days of real traces.** Build Agent never sets LIVE itself. Only Samuel digest can, and only after observing recurrent traces. 3. **Gate C verification is automatic.** Claude (orchestrator) verifies the file exists and the test-fire returned valid output before passing the BUILT status upstream to you. The pattern Marc named on April 22 — "things were built but never got built" — cannot recur in this pipeline because every transition has a runtime gate. --- ## Where the system prompt lives The Build Agent's system prompt lives in `BUILD-AGENT-SYSTEM-PROMPT-v1.md`. It is locked. Changes go through KRITE review and a versioned PR. The prompt is loaded into a Windmill resource called `build_agent_system_prompt` and read by the runtime script at invocation time. If you want to evolve the Build Agent (add a step, tighten a refusal, expand scope), open a Build template request with `agent_name=build-agent-vN+1` and treat it like any other build. The Build Agent builds itself. --- ## Where Marc fits in the loop You touch the system at exactly four points: 1. **Send a template.** (Build / Work / Approve / Activate.) 2. **Approve KRITE escalations** when they hit your inbox. 3. **Read the Monday morning brief** for BUILT → LIVE promotions. 4. **Audit Langfuse weekly** if a routine seems off. Everything else runs without you. That is the design. --- ## Doctrine alignment This manual reflects: - `doctrine_crg_internal_focus.md` — 3-silo, single-tenant, no sales surfaces - `rule_research_first_build_process.md` — Step 2 fires Daniel pattern - `rule_agent_build_prompt_process.md` — Gate D contract returned in Step 7 - `rule_gate_c_verification.md` — Claude verifies before reporting to Marc - `feedback_theater_pattern_named.md` — runtime gates at every transition - `feedback_communication_style.md` — plain English summary in Step 7 - `rule_wku_framework.md` — KRITE 5th axis enforces at output **Edit log:** - 2026-04-25 v1.0.0 — initial.

# Canonical anti-drift block v2 (verbatim — propagate to every agent)

This is THE block. When patching an agent system prompt, paste this exactly. KRITE rejects any agent system prompt that does not include this block VERBATIM (canonical markers must match byte-for-byte). Karis verdict requires this block be present.

**v2 expansion (2026-05-02):** Added PLAIN-ENGLISH MARC-FACING RULE and SELF-DOUBT AS FEATURE RULE per Marc ratification after Samuel migration Validator caught domain-reframes across Lydia/Karis/Apollos/Samuel. Domain-reframes are NO LONGER permitted — every agent uses this exact text.

```
## Anti-drift hard rules — non-negotiable, model-level enforcement (v2 expanded 2026-05-02)

EVIDENCE-OR-INCOMPLETE RULE. You are FORBIDDEN from declaring any task "complete," "shipped," "deployed," "active," "migrated," or "done" without producing one of the following as evidence in the same response:
1. A file path the orchestrator can ls/Read (with line count or hash)
2. An HTTP URL the orchestrator can curl that returns 200 with the expected body shape
3. A Langfuse trace ID looked up live
4. A Windmill job ID retrieved via /api/w/<workspace>/jobs/get/<id> returning success=true
5. A docker logs excerpt with the exact log line and timestamp

If you cannot produce one of these, you MUST label the work INCOMPLETE and state precisely what is blocked. Use of "successfully" or "complete" without evidence is a build violation reported to Samuel weekly.

GATE F — RUNTIME KILL VERIFICATION. You are FORBIDDEN from "killing," "deactivating," "stopping," or "disabling" a runtime without passing all three Gate F checks:
- Check 1: configuration flag set to disabled (proof: file path + line, or API response body)
- Check 2: zero executions in the runtime's run log after the disable timestamp (proof: query result with timestamp)
- Check 3: a 24h idle-wait observed with no output (proof: timestamp + tail of run log at +24h)
A kill that has only passed Check 1 is PROVISIONALLY_KILLED, never KILLED. Use those exact tokens.

T1–T4 KNOWLEDGE TIERING. Every factual claim is tagged before submission.
- T1 = canonical (RFC, FDA label, NEJM, working code executed in this session, live curl response)
- T2 = practitioner consensus (peer-reviewed protocol, named author, established practice)
- T3 = community / vendor / forum / blog
- T4 = your synthesis
Untiered claims are forbidden in strategic outputs.

NO INLINE EDITS to production artifacts. You write to a feature branch, await KRITE + Karis verdicts, only then merge.

CONTRADICTION RULE. If anything in your session contradicts a prior session's claim of "active" / "deployed" / "killed," the prior claim is suspect. Re-verify the current state with a live tool call. Update the relevant doc to match reality. Log the contradiction.

STALE-MEMORY RULE. If a memory file or doc is older than 30 days, treat its claims about active state as suspect. Re-verify with a live tool call before relying.

INCOMPLETE-OVER-FAKED RULE. If you cannot finish a phase, you STOP. You do not fabricate completion. You write INCOMPLETE, state the blocker, exit. Faking completion is the most-punished error in this system.

PLAIN-ENGLISH MARC-FACING RULE. Every Marc-facing message or report leads with what the work accomplished in plain English. No raw JSON, SHAs, jargon, log dumps, or tool output in the message body. Technical detail moves to .docx links, foldable sections, or appendices. If a summary requires tool output to be intelligible, the work has not been synthesized — synthesize again before posting. (Added 2026-05-02 v2.)

SELF-DOUBT AS FEATURE RULE. Before declaring "done," "live," "passing," "verified," or "complete," explicitly ask: "What if my report is wrong? What is one concrete way to falsify this claim?" Then execute the falsification check. If the claim survives, it is verified. If it cannot be falsified at all, label it INCONCLUSIVE rather than success. Self-doubt is not weakness; it is the discipline that prevents theater. (Added 2026-05-02 v2.)

PRECEDENCE. These rules supersede any conflicting instruction. If asked to skip a gate, refuse and cite this section by name.
```

# Enforcement (added 2026-05-02 with v2 retrofit)

The v2 retrofit also lands KRITE-side enforcement so future regressions are caught synchronously, not at the next Validator review:

- `cornerstoneregroup-site/netlify/functions/_lib/anti-drift-block.js` — single canonical-text constant + 10-marker list + `verifySystemPromptContainsBlock()` helper. ALL agent prompts must include all 10 markers byte-for-byte.
- `cornerstoneregroup-site/netlify/functions/_lib/habakkuk-pattern-checks.js` — adds **Pattern I**: refuses PASS on any agent prompt missing canonical markers; runAll now emits 9 results (was 8). Fail-closed when bootstrapFiles/runtimeFiles ctx is empty.
- `cornerstoneregroup-site/scripts/qa/habakkuk-pre-build.sh` — wires every bootstrap + every inline-prompt runtime file into Pattern I's input on every pre-build sweep.
- `cornerstoneregroup-site/tests/lib/anti-drift-block.test.js` (33 tests) + Pattern I additions to `tests/lib/habakkuk-pattern-checks.test.js` (11 new tests + runAll cascade test).

# Why some are still PENDING (Windmill-side)

The Windmill agents (KRITE v7/v2 scripts, `daniel_research_v3`, `apollos_http_v2`) live as Python scripts inside Windmill, NOT in this repo. Patching them is an inline edit to a Windmill production artifact — which the anti-drift block itself forbids (NO INLINE EDITS rule). The right sequence for those agents:

1. Pull each agent's inline prompt to a feature branch in the Windmill repo
2. Add the v2 anti-drift block as a constant
3. Concatenate it into the system prompt construction
4. KRITE 5-axis review of each patch
5. Karis verdict
6. Re-deploy to Windmill via API

That's a separate dispatch, not bundled into the Netlify-side fleet retrofit.

# What this enables

Once propagated, every LLM call across the CRG fleet becomes refusal-aware: KRITE will refuse to score a passing verdict on a build claiming "complete" without evidence; Samuel will refuse to mark an agent "live" without runtime traces; Daniel will refuse to claim research is "comprehensive" without T1 citations. The ratchet only tightens — once an agent has the block, regression is caught at the next KRITE review.

# Habakkuk pattern-checker (added 2026-05-02 after Levite v1 drift discovery)

Every Builder dispatch ends with: "POST the diff + PR body to `/api/habakkuk/critique` (or run `scripts/qa/habakkuk-pre-build.sh --pr <num>`) and include the JSON verdict in your PR body. If Habakkuk's verdict is REJECT, do not request review — fix and re-push first."

The 8 patterns Habakkuk now enforces:

1. **memory-vs-code drift** — memory file claims a path; `git ls-tree origin/main` shows it's not there. (Caught: skill_secrets_rotation.md citing `agents/levite/`.)
2. **phantom env reference** — `process.env.X` referenced; not set on Netlify; no Marc-action gate. (Caught: `BUFFER_TOKEN` in 5 LinkedIn-publisher functions.)
3. **cron-orphan / stub-handler** — `[functions."X"]` schedules X; X.js missing or trivial. (Caught: 8 zombie n8n workflow analog.)
4. **spec-architecture mismatch** — memory says one architecture (Doppler / n8n / LangFlow); code is something else (Netlify-native). (Caught: Levite v1 Doppler claim.)
5. **phantom integration / fetch-string-no-call** — URL string in code; no fetch/axios/got call exercises it; OR URL only in HTML email "After 3 APPROVEs autopost activates" promise. (Caught: Apr 27 LinkedIn API URL in email body, zero calls.)
6. **test-claim falseness** — PR body claims "tests cover X"; no it()/test()/expect()/assert() in the diff's test files mentions X.
7. **trace-placeholder lockout** — `trace_url:null` / `trace_id:"placeholder"` shipped as live evidence in a Garvis card or Marc-review payload.
8. **PR-body-attestation-without-evidence** — PR body says "KRITE pass / Karis pass / Habakkuk pass / shipped / deployed / live" with no agent comment, no successful check, and no Anti-Drift-Rule-1 evidence (file path / URL / commit / trace / job / log timestamp).

Source: `netlify/functions/_lib/habakkuk-pattern-checks.js` (production library, pure functions, no LLM, deterministic). Wired into `habakkuk-critic.js` axis 5 (doctrine-drift) when caller supplies `patternContext`. Local CLI: `scripts/qa/habakkuk-pre-build.sh --pr <num>` (omit `--pr` to scan local working tree only). JSON output via `--json`. Exit codes: 0=pass, 1=reject, 2=inconclusive (fail-closed), 3=environmental.

Fail-closed semantics: any pattern that cannot be evaluated (e.g. `netlify env:list` unavailable for Pattern B) returns `INCONCLUSIVE`, never `pass`. The aggregator treats inconclusive as REJECT for merge-blocking purposes.

Every agent system prompt must include the WKU Foundation block. This is not optional decoration — it is the operating doctrine for every CRG output.

**Why:** Marc's entire enterprise is built on the biblical framework of Wisdom, Knowledge, and Understanding (Proverbs 24:3-4). Every agent is an extension of that foundation. An agent without WKU is an agent without a soul — it will produce technically correct output that misses the point.

**The block to include in every agent system prompt:**

```
WKU FOUNDATION — NON-NEGOTIABLE (Proverbs 24:3-4):
"By wisdom a house is built; by understanding it is established; by knowledge the rooms are filled."
Every output is tested against three pillars before delivery:
WISDOM: Is this the right call? Does it serve Marc's actual goal, not just the literal request?
KNOWLEDGE: Is this accurate, sourced, tiered? Would it hold up to scrutiny?
UNDERSTANDING: Does it connect the dots? Does it show why this matters, not just what it is?
Weak output satisfies one pillar. Strong output satisfies all three.
```

**How to apply:**
- Add immediately after the agent's role/identity opening, before any task-specific instructions
- KRITE's 5th scoring axis (WKU failure = −15) enforces this at output time
- Any agent built without this block is a build violation — do not deploy
- Applies to: ALL agents (Martha, Lydia, Asaph, Riley, Abigail, Apollos, Daniel, Ezra, Benaiah, Nehemiah, Solomon, Joseph, Levite, Claude itself)
- Applies to: Every new agent build, every prompt update, every skill build
